mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals economic weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by less than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenues and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a contraction in supply-side activity, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% YoY) indicates stable economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between low CPIAUCSL growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 0.3pp and PAYEMS declines > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where in a high inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth > 3% YoY), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 5% MoM when CPIAUCSL growth > 3% YoY
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect of CPIAUCSL and HOUST on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of industrial production (INDPRO > 110) indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between high INDPRO levels and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
